questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 6 and 3024, respectively. If one of the numbers is 54, then find the other number.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

HCF = 6

LCM = 3024

One of the numbers = 54

**Concept: **

Product of two numbers = Product of their HCF and LCM.

**Solution:**

⇒ Let the other number be x.

⇒ So, according to the concept, 54x = 63024

⇒ x = (6 × 3024)/54

**Therefore, the other number is 336.**

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cylinder is 180 cm³, the area of its base is 30 cm² and the height is 6 cm then the diameter of the cylinder is (in cm):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Volume of the cylinder (V) = 180 cm³

Area of the base of the cylinder (A) = 30 cm²

**Concept: **

Diameter of the cylinder base can be found from the area of the base using the formula A = πr².

**Solution:**

⇒ The radius (r) can be calculated from the area formula as √(A/π).

⇒ Therefore, the diameter is 2 × √(A/π).

**Hence, the diameter of the cylinder is 2√{30/pi} .**

questions.question: Which of the following is divisible by 24?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Numbers are 2940, 2856, 1458, and 1860.

**Concept: **

A number is divisible by 24 if it is divisible by both 3 and 8 (factors of 24).

Divisibility of 3 = Sum of all the digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility of 8 = Last three digit is divisible by 8.

**Solution:**

Please note that all the options are divisible by 3 as the digit sum of all the options is divisible by 3.

So, by using the divisibility rule of 8, Only option 2, i.e. 2856, the last 3 digits is divisible by 8, so it will be divisible by 24.

**Hence, the number divisible by 24 is 2856.**

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can complete it in 16 days. If B works at 50 percent efficiency, then in how many days A and B together will complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete a work in 8 day
s.

A alone can complete it in 16 days.

B is working at 50 percent efficiency.

**Concept: **

Work = Rate x Time

**Solution:**

⇒ If A alone can complete the work in 16 days, A's work rate is 1/16.

⇒ If A and B together can complete the work in 8 days, their combined work rate is 1/8.

⇒ B's work rate is therefore (1/8 - 1/16) = 1/16.

⇒ If B is working at 50 percent efficiency, B's current work rate is 1/16 × 0.5 = 1/32.

⇒ Therefore, A and B's combined work rate is 1/16 + 1/32 = 3/32.

⇒ Hence, A and B together will complete the work in 1 / (3/32) days.

**Therefore, A and B together will complete the work in 32/3 days.**

questions.question: A sum of money is to be distributed among A, B and C in proportion of 5 ∶ 7 ∶ 11. If B gets Rs. 1,500 more than A, what is B’s share?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A ∶ B ∶ C = 5 ∶ 7 ∶ 11

B gets Rs. 1500 more than A.

**Concept:**

Proportional distribution

**Solution:**

⇒ The ratio of B to A is 7 : 5.

⇒ The difference in shares is 2 parts.

⇒ So, 2 parts = Rs. 1500, then 1 part = Rs. 1500 / 2.

⇒ Hence, B's share = 7 parts × (Rs. 1500 / 2).

**Therefore, B's share is Rs. 5250.**

**Concept: **

Third proportional = b²/a

Fourth proportional = bc/a

**Solution:**

According to the question, 

Third proportion = Fourth proportion

⇒ b2/a = bc/a

⇒ (18 × 18)/8 = 81(x2​ + 2x + 2)/2

⇒ 81/2 = 81(x2​ + 2x + 2)/2

⇒ (x2​ + 2x + 2) = 1

⇒ x2​ + x + x + 1 = 0

⇒ (x+1)(x + 1) = 0

⇒ x = -1

**Therefore, the value of x is -1.**

questions.question: The average of six consecutive odd numbers is 68. What is the cube of the difference between the highest and the lowest numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any n consecutive odd or even numbers, the difference between the highest and lowest number is always (n − 1) × 2.

Here, n = 6 numbers, so the Difference = (6 − 1) × 2 = 10.

The average value (68) does not affect the difference between the terms.

Required value = Cube of the difference = 10³ = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 6 consecutive odd numbers = 68

**Formula Used:**

Average of consecutive numbers in AP = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7afb80a127d7399c1129af2b17d989b5c85d69f9747d4c5b5742f91f0ecc7f20.png] 

For an even number of terms (6), the average lies exactly between the two middle terms.

⇒ Middle terms (3rd and 4th) = 68 − 1 and 68 + 1

⇒ 3rd term = 67, 4th term = 69

⇒ Full sequence of odd numbers: 63, 65, 67, 69, 71, 73

⇒ Lowest number = 63

⇒ Highest number = 73

⇒ Difference = 73 − 63 = 10

⇒ Cube of difference = 10³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

For any sequence in AP, the average is the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).

Difference between Extreme Terms

In a sequence of n terms with common difference d, the difference between the nth and 1st term is (n − 1) × d.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n odd natural numbers starting from 1 is always n².</p

questions.question: A seller announced 30% discount on the marked price of a fan. If the selling price of the fan is Rs. 2,800, then the marked price of the fan was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 30%

Selling price = Rs. 2800

**Concept: **

Selling price = Marked price - Discount

**Solution:**

⇒ The marked price of the fan = Selling price / (1 - Discount %)

⇒ The marked price of the fan = 2800 / (1 - 30%)

⇒ The marked price of the fan = 2800 / (7/10)

**Hence, the marked price of the fan was Rs. 4000.**

questions.question: Four cows are tied at 4 corners (one at each corner) of a rectangular field of length 30 m and width 20 m. The length of the rope is 7 m. What is the area of the field that cows CANNOT graze? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Area of rectangular field = 30 × 20 = 600 m²

Each corner of a rectangle is 90°, so 4 corners = 360° = 1 complete circle.

Grazed Area = Area of circle with radius 7 m = πr²

Grazed Area = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 m²

Ungrazed Area = Total Area − Grazed Area = 600 − 154 = 446 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 446 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of rectangular field (L) = 30 m

Width of rectangular field (W) = 20 m

Length of rope (radius, r) = 7 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = Length × Width

Area of a Sector = (θ/360) × πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20f1569d2597b04c2142eff3441d56d8df8ef5aed55843efbbe768c80493d364.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total area of the field = 30 × 20 = 600 m²

⇒ In a rectangle, the interior angle at each corner is 90°.

⇒ Area grazed by one cow = (90/360) × π × (7)²

⇒ Area grazed by one cow = (1/4) × (22/7) × 49 = 38.5 m²

⇒ Total grazed area by 4 cows = 4 × 38.5 = 154 m²

⇒ Area that cows cannot graze = Total area − Total grazed area

⇒ Area that cows cannot graze = 600 − 154 = 446 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 446 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Circle and Sectors

The area of a circle is πr². Since the sum of the angles at the corners of a rectangle is 360°, the four quadrants at the corners combine to form exactly one full circle.

General Polygon Case

If cows are tied at the corners of any quadrilateral (not just a rectangle), the sum of the interior angles is always 360°, so the total grazed area will still be πr² if the ropes are of equal length.

Perimeter of Grazed Region

The total boundary length of the grazed area inside the field is equivalent to the circumference of one circle, which is 2πr.</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 58% of the votes polled is elected by a majority of 4,032 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner's share = 58%

Loser's share = 100% − 58% = 42%

Difference (Majority) = 58% − 42% = 16%

16% of total votes = 4032

Total votes = (4032 ÷ 16) × 100 = 252 × 100 = 25200

**∴ The correct answer is 25,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Winning candidate's vote share = 58%

Majority (Difference in votes) = 4,032

 
 
 Total Votes = 100%

 
 
 Winner = 58%

 
 
 Loser = 42%

 
 

 

 
 
 Majority (Diff) = 16% = 4032
 
 
 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of votes polled be x.

⇒ Votes secured by the winner = 58% of x

⇒ Votes secured by the loser = (100% − 58%) of x = 42% of x

⇒ Majority = Winner's votes − Loser's votes

⇒ 58% of x − 42% of x = 16% of x

⇒ 16% of x = 4032

⇒ (16 ÷ 100) × x = 4032

⇒ x = (4032 × 100) ÷ 16

⇒ x = 252 × 100

⇒ x = 25,200

**∴ The correct answer is 25,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election with Invalid Votes

If some votes are declared invalid, then Valid Votes = Total Polled Votes − Invalid Votes. The winner and loser percentages are usually calculated on the total valid votes unless stated otherwise in the problem.

Finding the Base Value

When a specific percentage of a base quantity is known, the total base value can be found directly using the formula: Total Base = (Given Value × 100) ÷ Percentage Part.

Multi-Candidate Elections

In an election involving three or more candidates, the final "margin of victory" or majority is always calculated as the absolute difference in the total votes between the first-placed (winning) candidate and the second-placed candidate.

questions.question: After a discount of 15% on the marked price, the profit is 5%. What percent discount on the marked price be there to have 8% profit (rounded off to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount on marked price = 15%

Profit = 5%

Desired profit = 8%

**Concept:**

Profit % = [(Selling price - Cost price) / Cost price] × 100

Selling price = Marked Price - Discount

Selling price = Marked Price × (100 - Discount%)/100

Cost Price = Selling price × 100/(100 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be Rs.100.

Selling Price = 100 × (100 - 15)/100 = Rs. 85

Cost Price = 85 × 100/(100 + 5) = 80.95

When 8% profit is given,

New Selling Price = 80.95 × 108/100 = Rs. 87.42

Discount = 100 - 87.42 = 12.58 

Discount% = Discount/MP × 100

⇒ 12.58/100 × 100 = 12.58 or 12.6%

**Therefore 12.6 percent discount on the marked price be there to have 8% profit.**

questions.question: The difference between compound and simple interests on a certain sum of money at the interest rate of 20% per annum for 1{1 over2} years is Rs. 6,200, when the interest is compounded semi-annually. Find the sum of money.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The difference between CI and SI = Rs. 6200

Time = 1{1 over2} years

Rate = 20%

Compounded semi-annually

**Concept Used:**

SI = PRT/100

CI = P{[1 + R/100]T - 1}

where, P = Principal

R = Rate of interest

T = Time period

**Calculation:**

SI = (P × 20 × 3)/(100 × 2)

⇒ SI = 3P/10

As the Interest is compounded semiannually, R = 20/2 = 10% and Time period = 3

⇒ CI = P{[1 + 10/100]³ - 1}

⇒ CI = P{[1 + 1/10]3 - 1}

⇒ CI = P{[11/10]3 - 1}

⇒ CI = 331P/1000

According to Question,

⇒ CI - SI = 6200

⇒ 331P/1000 - 3P/10 = 6200

⇒ (331P - 300P)/1000 = 6200

⇒ 31P/1000 = 6200

⇒ P = 200000

**Therefore, the sum of money is Rs. 200000.**

questions.question: In 4 h, a boat goes 12 km along the stream. It covers 6 km against the stream in the same time. The speed of the boat in still water (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In 4 h, a boat goes 12 km along the stream.

It covers 6 km against the stream in the same time.

**Concept: **

Speed = Distance / Time

**Solution:**

The speed of the boat along the stream = Distance / Time = 12 km / 4 h = 3 km/h.

The speed of the boat against the stream = Distance / Time = 6 km / 4 h = 1.5 km/h.

Speed of the boat in still water = (Speed along the stream + Speed against the stream) / 2

⇒ (3 + 1.5)/2 = 2.25 km/h

**Therefore, the speed of the boat in still water is 2.25 km/h.**
